topics.topic: Ownership and enforcement boundary for INV-18 conflict-copy exclusion during placement
questions: How can `source_folder` own the part of INV-18 stating that a conflict copy is not placed while it is expressly forbidden to own whether a photo was placed; does `source_folder` own only conflict-name eligibility, does `photo_delivery` own the placement guarantee, or is the prohibition meant to have an exception?

Which `source_folder` capability structurally guarantees the placement half of INV-18, including a file whose name changes after observation: must `read_source_bytes` revalidate the ignored-name rule, must `observe_source_files` return an opaque observation that can be read safely, or must `photo_delivery` know and repeat the conflict-name rule; and which direct dependency symbols must `photo_delivery` import?

How can `source_folder` own all of INV-18, including whether a photo is placed, when its module contract says it must not own whether a photo was placed or published; must the invariant be split, assigned to `photo_delivery`, or defined as guaranteed solely through source eligibility?

quotes: | A1 | order 1 to 8, ignored names, walking order | `source_folder` |
| A1 | order 9 to 11, placed and published status | `photo_delivery` |
- ignored names, links, the settling time, source limits and file signatures;
- reading the bytes of one source file without following a link;
- whether a photo was placed or published;
- one placement per project and content, replay, and per-photo failure;
judgement.why: The texts assign conflict-name eligibility and safe source reading to source_folder, assign the placement decision to photo_delivery, and explicitly declare the two source_folder symbols that photo_delivery imports; source_folder can therefore own INV-18 by making conflict copies ineligible without owning placement records or placement status.
